title: Result of config.apply (v1.0)
description: Request args: {"set": {key: value, ...}} with 1 to 16 keys, and "dry": true for the one key battery.guard (a dry run, OPERATIONS.md). Every key, value and authorization is checked before any is written; a failed check answers invalid or refused with error "<reason>:<key>" and nothing is written. Writes are then made in order; a write that still fails is reported here and the others stand. With args.confirm ({"within_s": 30..900}, default 300) the change is tentative (OPERATIONS.md section 3.4): the result also names the job, and a failed write reverts the others at once. A repeat of a confirm request whose job is already known (a retry after a reboot cleared the id cache) runs nothing and answers that job's summary instead, {job, op, state, owed}, as job.get does.

dry.description: A dry run (args.dry, battery.guard only, since v0.3.12): nothing was written, battery_guard says what the guard would do, and applied, complete, reboot_needed and restarting are absent. Otherwise applied, complete, reboot_needed and restarting are always present.

refusal.description: When not accepted: the rule that refuses the value.

would_sleep.description: About a later release: this one never sleeps.

applied.description: key -> ok | failed. Never the value.

restarting.description: A write (connectivity.mode) makes the device restart shortly after this result.

job.description: With confirm: the job's identity, for job.get, job.confirm and job.cancel.

reverted.description: With confirm, when a write failed: whether what did apply was put back.
